title: Boolean function
summary: A Boolean function maps inputs from a two-element set ({true, false} or {0,1}) to an output in the same set. It is defined by its arity k, producing one of 2^(2^k) possible functions. Core operations include NOT, AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR, and XNOR. Complex functions such as majority or cryptographic S-boxes extend these basics. Representations include truth tables, Karnaugh maps, binary decision diagrams, and algebraic normal forms. Properties range from constant and monotone to balanced, bent, and correlation-immune. Derived concepts involve Shannon cofactors, Boolean derivatives, Möbius transforms, and Walsh spectra used in cryptanalysis.

mechanisms.title: Truth-table and algebraic representation
mechanisms.explanation: A Boolean function with k arguments has 2^k possible inputs, each mapped to 0 or 1, yielding 2^(2^k) distinct functions. It can be explicitly listed as a truth table or expressed algebraically using AND, OR, NOT, and XOR in forms such as disjunctive normal form or algebraic normal form (Zhegalkin polynomial).

mechanisms.title: Cryptographic analysis via Walsh and autocorrelation transforms
mechanisms.explanation: The Walsh transform decomposes the function into linear parity components; its maximum coefficient measures linearity. The autocorrelation function evaluates output changes under input perturbations; maximal coefficients indicate the propagation criterion. These transforms are foundational in assessing resistance to linear and differential cryptanalysis.
